name: DISC
description: DISC returns the discount rate for a bond or Treasury bill based on its price, redemption value, and time to maturity.
tldr: Calculates the discount rate for a security.

basicExample.description: Discount rate for a Treasury bill
basicExample.explanation: A T-bill priced at $95 that redeems at $100 in one year has a discount rate of about 5.26%.

advancedExamples.title: With actual/360 basis
advancedExamples.explanation: Basis 2 counts actual days and uses a 360-day year.

howItWorks: DISC calculates the annual discount rate using the formula (redemption - pr) / redemption * (days per year / days to maturity). It is commonly used for short-term instruments.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: Price and redemption are per $100 face value.
Basis affects the day count and year length.

commonErrors.fix: Use DATE function or valid date serial numbers.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: DISC works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between DISC and YIELD?
faq.answer: DISC is for discount instruments. YIELD is for coupon-paying bonds.

faq.question: When is DISC used?
faq.answer: It is used for Treasury bills and commercial paper that are priced at a discount.
